name: Mariaccio
description: Mariaccio is a spirited Italian card game from the Neapolitan tradition, specifically a variation of Briscola. It is also known as 'Marianna' or 'Mariaggia' (when played with open cards). The defining feature is the 'Marriage' (Mariaccio)â€”a King and Knight of the same suitâ€”which grants bonus points. It is a game of high targets, usually requiring 250 points to win, making it a longer and more tactical experience than standard Briscola.

history.origins: Derived from the merging of Briscola mechanics with the 'Marriage' (King-Queen) bonuses of the Mariagespiel family.
timeline: 1800s: Briscola-based marriage games spread through Southern Italy.
1920s: The name 'Mariaccio' becomes common in Naples and surrounding provinces.
Present: A staple of Neapolitan cafe culture and family gatherings.
20th Century: Variations for 4 players (partnerships) emerged, but the 2-player game remains the classic.
history.cultural: In Naples, 'Mariaccio' is often played with a sense of theater and loud 'Accuse' declarations.
history.evolution: The game moved from a 60-point target to a 250-point target to allow the 'Accuse' (marriages) to decide the outcome rather than just high cards.

setup.players: Two players. Five cards are dealt to each player; the eleventh card is placed face up on the table to determine the trump suit. The remaining stock is placed face down across the face-up trump. The non-dealer leads to the first trick.
setup.deck: 40 cards. Ranking: Ace, 3, King, Knight, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 5 cards. A trump card is turned up to set the 'Briscola' suit.

rules.objective: Score 250 points through tricks and 'Mariaccio' declarations.
rules.gameplay: Standard Briscola rules: No obligation to follow suit or trump. High card wins. Winner draws first, then loser, until deck is empty.
keyRules: No obligation to follow suit or trump. High card of led suit wins, or highest trump if any. Winner of trick draws first from stock, then loser. Declare Mariaccio (King and Knight of same suit) when playing one of them for bonus points (40 trump, 20 non-trump). First to 250 points wins.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the marriage. A single Trump Marriage (40 pts) is worth more than a natural Ace and 3 combined (21 pts). If you have a King and Knight, save them until you need to snatch the lead.
strategy.intermediate: The Lead Management: Don't lead your high point cards (Aces/3s) unless you are sure they won't be trumped. Use small cards (2s/4s) to 'bait' out your opponent's high cards before playing your Mariaccio.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Holding: If your opponent has a high score and is close to 250, try to empty their trump reserves early. Without trumps, their marriages in other suits can still be trumped by you, nullifying their bonus point potential.
tips: Memory: You MUST track the remaining points in the deck as you approach 250. If there are no Aces/3s left, it's very hard to catch up without a marriage.
Call Out: Be bold with the 250-point call. If you are at 240 and you take a King (4 pts) of trumps, you are at 244 plus potentially secret marriages.

scoring.description: Card points from tricks (Ace 11, 3 10, King 4, Knight 3, Jack 2, 7-2 zero) plus Mariaccio bonuses (40 for trump marriage, 20 for non-trump).
